data.title: Valley of Aosta: Snowstorm, Avalanche, and Thunderstorm

thumbnail.alt_text: A work made of oil on canvas.

data.publication_history:
William Frost and Henry Reevem A Complete Catalogue of the Paintings, Water-Colour Drawings, Drawings, and Prints, in the Collection of the Late Hugh Andrew Johnstone Munroe, Esq., of Novar, at the Time of his Death Deposited in his House, no, 6, Hamilton Place, London (London, 1865), 95 no. 45.

"The James Price Pictures: A Sensational Day's Sale," Sydney Morning Herald, July 30, 1895, p. 7.

Ian Warrell, ed., J.M.W. Turner, exh. cat. (London: Tate Publishing, 2007)
data.exhibition_history:
New York Public Library, William Wadsworth and the Age of English Romanticism, October 27, 1987 - January 2, 1988; Bloomington, Indiana, Indiana University Art Gallery, January 27-March 6, 1988; Chicago Historical Society, April 6-June 5, 1988.

Washington, DC, National Gallery of Art, J.M.W. Turner, October 1, 2007-January 6, 2008; Dallas Museum of Art, February 10-May 28, 2008; New York, Metropolitan Museum of Art, June 24-September 21, 2008.
data.provenance_text: Probably Joseph Gillott (1799–1872), Birmingham, by Mar. 1845. Consigned to George Pennell (1796–1864). Hugh Andrew Johnson Munro of Novar (1797–1864), London, by 1848; sold, his sale, Christie’s, London, Apr. 6, 1878, lot 102 to Edward Montagu-Stuart-Wortley-Mackenzie, 1st Earl of Wharncliffe for 910 gns; Edward Montagu-Stuart-Wortley-Mackenzie, 1st Earl of Wharncliffe (1827–1899), until at least 1889. James Price, Paignton, England; sold, Christie’s, London, June 15, 1895, lot 66 to Thomas Agnews and Sons as agent for Sir Donald Currie for 4000 gns [annotated sale catalogue in curatorial object file. See also Sydney Morning Herald July 30, 1865]; Sir Donald Currie (1825–1909); by descent to his granddaughter, Margaret Celia Craven (1891–1987; born Margaret Mirrielees), Haslemere, England; sold to Thomas Agnews and Sons, July 29, 1947 [letter from Gabriel Naughton, Agnews, Mar. 19, 1993; in curatorial object file]; sold through Roland, Browse and Delbanco to the Art Institute of Chicago, 1947.
